names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 mai, «Sfântul Proroc Isaia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Μαΐου, «Προφήτης Ησαΐας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's heading for the Julian 9 May, „Свети пророк Исаија.“ — Свети left off, which is not a rank, and пророк left off, which is the `prophet` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back. Nothing else is in the heading: the royal kin, Jerusalem, Amos and the seven hundred years are all in the body. The form folds with `isaiah-the-egyptian`, which holds the same bare Исаија, and that fold is recorded as deliberate in the run's findings.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 9 mai — «Sfântul Proroc Isaia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Μαΐου — «Προφήτης Ησαΐας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and it is the Isaiah of the prophetic book, whom the page calls «ο πρώτος μεταξύ των τεσσάρων μεγάλων Προφητών». **He is none of the Isaiahs the name sweep raised** — of Kykkos, of Valaam, the Egyptian. **`dates` are added where the folder had none**, as a birth about 774 BC: the head line gives «(-774 - ;)» and the body «γεννήθηκε στα Ιεροσόλυμα περί το 774 π.Χ.», and the page gives no year at all for his death, only that he was sawn in two under Manasseh, so no death interval is recorded. **The Greek adds what the folder lacked**: his father Amos; Jerusalem as his birthplace; the Hebrew form of the name and its sense, «ο Θεός σώζει»; the rabbinic traditions about his kinship with Amaziah and Manasseh, which the page itself calls «θρύλοι μάλλον και όχι ιστορικές αλήθειες»; his marriage and his two sons and the meaning of their symbolic names, Jasoub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz; his call in 738 BC in the last year of Uzziah and the first of Jotham; the vision in the temple and the coal from the altar; the reigns his work spanned; the wooden saw; the title «Ευαγγελικός Προφήτης»; the translation of his relic to Constantinople under Theodosius II and its laying in the church of the martyr Laurence near the Blachernae; and a fragment of his skull at the monastery of Chilandar on Athos. **Two hymns are stored, both proper and both naming him**; the page prints a second apolytikion in Ἦχος β’ as well, which is left in the source. `types` are not changed: the kontakion's «προφητομάρτυς» is a hymn's word and the corpus's `prophet` is what the calendars give.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.05.2026 (9. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети пророк Исаија.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, and the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep him on, so nothing moved. **A `floruit` is added where the folder held only a birth**: „Живео и пророковао на седам стотина година пре Христа“ — he lived and prophesied seven hundred years before Christ — which is this book's only date and names no event but the prophesying itself, so it goes in its own key and neither touches nor narrows saint.gr's birth of about 774 BC. The round number stands in the bounds and its roundness in the note, as the Julian 1 May of this wave did with Jeremiah's „шест стотина година“. **The Prologue states as fact what saint.gr calls a legend**: that this great prophet „беше од царскога рода“, born at Jerusalem of his father Amos, the brother of Amaziah king of Judah, where the Greek page calls the same kinship „θρύλοι μάλλον και όχι ιστορικές αλήθειες“. Nothing was chosen; both readings stand in the life. **New here and in no other book read for this folder**: that he walked three days wholly naked through the streets of Jerusalem, foretelling the city's imminent fall under the Assyrian king Sennacherib and warning the king and the chiefs of the people not to lean on the help of the Egyptians and the Ethiopians, since those too would soon be subdued by that same Sennacherib, but on the help of God the Most High; and that this prophecy, like all the rest, was fulfilled to the letter. The vision of the Lord of Sabaoth among the six-winged Seraphim, the spring of Siloam and its gloss „послата“, the comparison of Manasseh's generation with Sodom and Gomorrah, and the sawing in two outside Jerusalem the folder already held from the Romanian and the Greek, and they agree. `types` are not touched: Свети is no rank and пророк is the `prophet` the folder already carries. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: A prorocului Tău Isaia, pomenirea, Doamne, prăznuind, printr-însul Te rugăm, mântuieşte sufletele noastre.

english.text: Keeping the memory of thy prophet Isaiah, O Lord, we entreat thee through him: save our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς σάλπιγξ πανεύσημος, μεγαλοφώνω φθογγή, τῷ κόσμῳ προήγγειλας, τὴν παρουσίαν Χριστοῦ, Προφῆτα θεσπέσιε, σὺ γὰρ τοῦ Παρακλήτου, ἑλλαμφθεῖς τὴ δυνάμει, κάλαμος ὀξυγράφος, τῶν μελλόντων ἐδείχθης, διὸ σὲ Ἠσαΐα, ὕμνοις γεραίρομεν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, the second of two on the page of «Προφήτης Ησαΐας»; the first, in Ἦχος β’, is the general one for a prophet and is left in the source

english.text: As an all-glorious trumpet, with a great-voiced sound, thou didst announce beforehand to the world the coming of Christ, O divinely-speaking Prophet; for being illumined by the power of the Comforter thou wast shown to be a swift-writing reed of things to come, and therefore we honour thee, O Isaiah, with hymns.

hymns.text: Τῆς Προφητείας τὸ χάρισμα δεδεγμένος, προφητομάρτυς Ἡσαΐα θεοκήρυξ, πᾶσιν ἐτράνωσας τοῖς ὑφ᾽ ἤλιον, τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ φωνήσας μεγαλοφώνως σάρκωσιν· Ἱδοὺ ἡ Παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τήν ἐν πρεσβείαις ἀκοίμητον, on the page of «Προφήτης Ησαΐας»

english.text: Having received the gift of prophecy, O prophet-martyr Isaiah, herald of God, thou didst make plain to all that are under the sun the incarnation of God, crying it with a great voice: behold, the Virgin shall conceive in her womb.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο Προφήτης Ησαΐας, υιός του Αμώς, γεννήθηκε στα Ιεροσόλυμα περί το 774 π.Χ.», and the head line of the same page gives «(-774 - ;)». The page gives no year for his death and leaves that half of the head line blank, so no death interval is recorded.

floruit.note: The Ohrid Prologue, for the Julian 9 May: „Живео и пророковао на седам стотина година пре Христа.“ — a round number, and the only date this book gives him; it names no event but the living and the prophesying, so it is recorded as a floruit and not as a birth or a death. It does not conflict with the birth about 774 BC above, which saint.gr gives and which this book does not print; saint.gr puts his call about 738 BC. The hedge is the roundness of the number itself and it is recorded here rather than in the display, as the Julian 1 May of this wave did with Jeremiah's „шест стотина година“.
